chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Early touring details: Bill Bailey's name and border-town dates
summary: Bill Bailey's Troubadours took its name from the song about 1906-08; from Douglas the duo played Mexican border towns with just piano and drums.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You mentioned...uh...Bill Bailey's Troubadours. That Bill Bailey wasn't the same Bill Bailey that was...
No, they took it from the song, "Bill Bailey, Won't You Please Come Home."
...cause I thought it would be too early for Pearl Bailey's brother Bill. He was younger than that.
Oh, no, no. This was around 1906, 1907 or '8. They's...was right after the song, you know--"Bill Bailey, Won't You Please Come Home," so they called it Bill Bailey's Troubadours.
Uh, I see. You mentioned when you were working out of Douglas, Arizona, you played in Mexico sometimes.
Yeah, you know, border towns like Tijuana here. We played Cananea there and Naco and Agua Prieta. See, those were just across the border.
Did you do the same routine...the same act... the same music and everything?
No, just piano and drums. We didn't carry all that junk over there. We didn't have it.
